title: Customers and helpers
summary: Customers in Supermarket Simulator are generated and tracked while they shop, and the shop can gain helpers that take on the checkout so you are not the only one serving.
body: Customers are produced by the game rather than placed by hand, which is why the shop fills up on its own once the doors are open.
The game gives helpers their own controllable role, so a helper is a distinct thing from a hired cashier rather than a reskin of one.
Helpers can be put on checkout duty, which is why the checkout logic is separate from who is standing there.
What this entry does not tell you: how many customers arrive, how patient they are, or what a helper costs. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Customers are generated by the game.
The game defines a controllable helper distinct from a cashier.
A helper can be put on checkout work.
The checkout interacts with a specific customer at a time.
The build keeps a skin and an avatar entry for each customer it generates.
Customers stand at a queue position of their own in the shop.
There is an ice-cream helper with a dress material and a hat material of its own.
